newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan police arrest man for killing MP.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan police arrest man for killing MP.

text.p: Sri Lankan police said on Wednesday they had arrested a man involved in the killing of an opposition United National Party parliamentarian earlier this month.

Mohammed Moharoof and five others, including a four-year-old boy, were gunned down by suspected Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels on a highway near the eastern port town of Trincomalee on July 20.
A police spokesman in Trincomalee, 250 km (156 miles) northeast of the capital Colombo, said the arrested man had confessed to having participated in Moharoof's assassination.
He said the man, whose identity was not disclosed, had told police that 25 LTTE fighters in three groups had ambushed Moharoof's jeep between Trincomalee and the nearby beach resort of Nilaveli.
The arrested man had said Moharoof was killed because he was seen to be supporting the ruling People's Alliance devolution package aimed at giving more powers to minorities.
Police have said Moharoof was travelling in the Moslem-dominated area around Trincomalee, and was on his way to a village where the LTTE had kidnapped fishermen in recent weeks when he was killed.
Moharoof was the second parliamentarian to be assassinated in Trincomalee this month.
Arunasalam Thangathurai, a lawmaker of the Tamil United National Front, was killed in Trincomalee in a grenade attack on July 5 after he had inaugurated a new school building.
The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, which erupted in 1983. The LTTE put the toll higher.
